title: Lesson 3 Quiz: Wages, Minimum Wage, and Labor Policy
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it completes the lesson's quiz requirement, and your score is recorded separately.

questions.prompt: In the simple competitive model, what happens when a minimum wage is set above the equilibrium wage?

choices.text: Employers hire more workers, because the higher wage attracts applicants
More people want jobs than employers want to fill, a surplus of labor
Employers want more workers than are available, a shortage of labor
Nothing changes, because the market wage adjusts to the new minimum

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: In a market for hotel housekeepers, labor demand is L_d = 1,100 − 35W and labor supply is L_s = 140 + 45W, where W is the hourly wage in dollars. A minimum wage of $15 per hour is introduced. According to the simple competitive model, how many fewer housekeepers are employed than at the equilibrium without a minimum wage? (Enter a number only, in workers.)

Hypothetical example: Study X finds that a minimum wage increase in Town X caused almost no job losses. Study Y finds clear job losses after an increase in Town Y. Other things equal, which difference between the towns best fits the factors economists point to when explaining why results differ?

choices.text: Town X's employers may have had less power to set wages than Town Y's
Town X's new minimum may have been far above its local wages, unlike Town Y's
Town X's new minimum may have been close to its local wages, unlike Town Y's
Town X's labor demand may have been more responsive to wages than Town Y's

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A town's only large employer is a monopsonist. It pays $12 per hour and hires 300 workers. The labor supply curve it faces slopes upward and crosses its labor demand curve at a wage of $15 and 400 workers (the competitive outcome). In the standard monopsony model, which minimum wage would lead the employer to hire the most workers?

Hypothetical example: In a region, many former coal miners are unemployed because the new job openings are in health care and need different skills. Which policy targets the main cause of this unemployment most directly?

choices.text: A retraining program that teaches skills used in health care
A website that lists current job openings in the region
A higher minimum wage for health care jobs in the region
Longer unemployment benefits for the former coal miners
